newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Ex-USDA Brazil coffee rep to continue forecasting.
newsitem.headline: Ex-USDA Brazil coffee rep to continue forecasting.

text.p: The former representative of the U.S Department of Agriculture (USDA) responsible for field surveys of Brazilian coffee output is to continue producing crop forecasts for private clients.
Leon Yallouz left the USDA in May this year when the U.S. Agriculture Counsellor in Brazil decided to close down the Foreign Agriculture Service in Rio de Janeiro.
He has decided however to continue working as a private consultant and has just returned from a 20-day field trip to Brazil's coffee regions.
"I will be doing three field trips a year, the same as when I was with the USDA," Yallouz told Reuters.
"One I have just completed, the second will take place in January/February and the final trip will be in April/May. A crop forecast and survey will follow each trip," he said.
The first forecast will be available to clients from mid-November, Yallouz said.
Yallouz last estimated the 1996/97 Brazilian coffee crop at 27.5 million 60-kg bags, a forecast widely used as a benchmark in the absence of an official government crop survey.
The government has already said that it is hoping to have an official estimate for the 1997/98 crop and producers say a forecast could be ready by the end of next month.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
